title: feat: guard reads, web templates and base-copy lessons
headline: The guards pass a read loop piped on and a printed PowerShell string, a body that claims a measured move must show Visuals, the app templates install only where a project shows a UI, and a build opens its PR as a draft after the first commit.
alignment: v1.45.0 is build 19 of the v2.0 plan: K145, K146 to K149 and the last piece of T13, each reproduced on the released 1.44.0 first.

items.text: The guards pass a read loop over guard files piped on to a reader (wc, head, tail, grep, sort with no output file), from a plain cd too; a pipe to a writer, a shell or a file, and a wildcard matching a dash-named file, are held.
items.where: A read loop over guard files piped to wc
items.after: Runs; a pipe to a writer is still held

items.text: A PowerShell statement that is one quoted string, beside a kit script, is read as printing it; a substitution or redirect in it keeps the strict reading.
items.where: A PowerShell loop printing a header before each kit script call

items.text: A for loop held for how its glob is read says so and how to rerun it, instead of naming the first protected place checked (a guard write was refused as a transcript write).
The Standard PR and release notes audits need a Visuals section when a body claims a measured move (a size, tokens, time or dollars across an arrow or a Summary row); tallies never count.
items.where: A PR body that says a size moved
items.after: Fails until the Visuals section is there

items.text: The component spec and component security checklist install only where the project shows a UI (a UI framework in package.json, or a components folder), with `--with-templates web`, or where a copy is already in place.
items.where: Installing the kit into a project with no UI

items.text: A build pushes its branch and opens its PR as a draft right after the first commit, so main's checks run on the branch from the first push; it stays a draft until the sweep, and a done feature runs its sweep before anything else on its PR.
The plan file and the plan gap check ask whether main's checks can read the branch, and a check change it needs ships first as its own small PR.
The test check names a changed test file main cannot load once, with the module main lacks, instead of each of its tests as failing; it still fails the run.

verification: Each row was reproduced on a throwaway clone of the released 1.44.0 before any change.
The new Visuals check, run over the last ten PR bodies, flags PR 55 and PR 51 only.
The guard tests hold every write twin beside each read the build lets through.

decisions.decision: A quoted wildcard stays a wildcard to the launcher
decisions.why: It reads a command both as the shell splits it and as plain text, so a reading it gets wrong only adds a check; a quoted regex in node -e code is held, and stays a named limit.

decisions.decision: A copy already in place keeps both app templates
decisions.why: Install never retires a template a project may be using; a project that wants them gone deletes them.
Install copies a different set of templates, and every project's PR audit gains a check.

upgrading: Install user and install project as usual. A project with no UI keeps the component templates it already has; delete them by hand if unused. Add `--with-templates web` to install project to get them where no UI shows yet.
limits: The launcher still reads a wildcard inside quotes, so a quoted regex such as /\*\*/ in inline node code can hold a read. The Visuals check reads arrows and Summary rows; a move told only in a sentence is not seen. During the fixes, local runs went wider than the rule (four extra guard test files, about 170 tests) until the owner stopped them; a check that keeps local runs to the changed tests is a list row for the next build.
